# Normally displayed final: formula text projection

Deterministic text projection of the normally displayed final, preserving its mathematical annotations. This is not an acquired original proof, implementation, or independent review document. Raw visible text and private formula DOM are preserved separately.

I completed a conditional bridge from the protected physical operations to conventional coherent fault correction—including repairs that read returning memory after a source becomes damaged. The decisive change was to use a representation in which individual fault amplitudes need not be normalized physical operations.

The construction

Fix each physical source’s decomposition into its logical qubit and its remaining gauge degrees of freedom. Keep those gauges, retired sources, controllers, records and returning environments in the complete memory. The clean-sector contribution to a location then has the form $G_j=U_j\otimes T_j,\qquad \|T_j\|\le 1.$ 

Here  $U_j$  is the intended logical gate.  $T_j$  may be a strict contraction. The actual operation remains an isometry; its residual  $B_j=W_j-G_j$  acts only on the location’s active logical wires and complete memory.

This matters because a perfectly acquired repair can still import memory information on a damaged input. In the new representation, that action remains a fault amplitude at the repair’s actual location. The earlier normalized causal counterexample remains valid: no later interaction has been deleted or moved backward.

Conventional fault-tolerance theory already supplies the Pauli-linearity and inclusion–exclusion machinery for handling such nonphysical amplitudes. I used that machinery directly. The new bridge establishes how our physical restoration theorem supplies its local support and complete marked-set bounds, without imposing a source-only decoder on every repair. arxiv.org+1

Given one common coherent outer decoder that corrects the declared benign fault paths, the construction aggregates the remaining bad amplitude into a bound  $\epsilon$ . It then produces a normalized reference on the same complete output memory: $\left\|Z-U_{\mathrm{target}}\otimes V\right\|\le 2\epsilon.$
